scenario.description: An underwriting manager must decide whether to launch a supplier's receivables-financing program and finalize the eligible invoice pool, reserve, disclosure, and monitoring terms, with input from compliance and client coverage.

shared_context.S1: A manufacturing supplier has requested a receivables-financing program against $3,000,000 of submitted commercial invoices.
shared_context.S2: The proposed invoices have stated payment terms of 60 days, and the supplier wants funding available before its next payroll date.
shared_context.S3: Maya makes the binding underwriting decision for the program.
shared_context.S4: The team's normal pre-launch process is a short underwriting huddle in which compliance and client coverage provide their final checks before Maya records the terms.
shared_context.S5: For the approval record, eligible_invoice_amount_usd means the total invoice amount eligible for financing after all exclusions but before any dilution reserve is applied; the dilution reserve is tracked separately in dilution_reserve_percent.

PF1.text: While reviewing the KYC file this morning, Jonas confirmed that $600,000 of the submitted invoices are owed by an entity beneficially owned by the supplier's chief executive; internal policy excludes related-party receivables from financing and requires a related-party disclosure in the approval record. Jonas received the ownership memo this morning, but it has not yet been circulated.

PF2.text: Elena received buyer confirmations yesterday showing that another $300,000 of the submitted invoices is under a documented delivery dispute and must be removed from the eligible pool; the confirmed undisputed invoices require a 15% dilution reserve, and coverage will provide a monthly buyer-confirmation report after launch. Elena has not yet attached the confirmations to the underwriting file.

acceptance_conditions: The receivables-financing program must be approved.
The eligible invoice pool must be exactly $2,100,000 before applying the dilution reserve.
A 15% dilution reserve must be applied separately to the eligible invoice pool.
The related-party receivables must be disclosed in the approval record.
A monthly buyer-confirmation monitoring commitment must be included, assigned to Elena or coverage.

content_checks.C5: any('monthly buyer-confirmation' in c['detail'] and (c['target'] == 'Elena' or c['target'] == 'A3' or c['target'] == 'coverage') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: PF1 removes exactly $600,000 of related-party invoices from the submitted $3,000,000 pool, changing the eligible amount from $2,700,000 after the other exclusion to exactly $2,100,000, and turns the related-party disclosure from false or unspecified to true.

PF2 removes exactly $300,000 of disputed invoices, changes the required dilution reserve to exactly 15%, and adds the monthly buyer-confirmation commitment needed to monitor the remaining $2,100,000 pool.
